decision.summary: The Federal Reserve decided to keep the target range for the federal funds rate at 1/4 to 1/2 percent.

changes.quote: Job gains were strong in June following weak growth in May.
changes.explanation: The Fed noted that job growth bounced back strongly in June after a weak showing in May.

changes.quote: Household spending has been growing strongly but business fixed investment has been soft.
changes.explanation: Consumers are spending at a healthy pace, but businesses are holding back on investments.

changes.quote: Near-term risks to the economic outlook have diminished.
changes.explanation: The Committee feels that immediate dangers to the economy have decreased.

changes.quote: Voting against the action was Esther L. George, who preferred at this meeting to raise the target range for the federal funds rate to 1/2 to 3/4 percent.
changes.explanation: One official dissented because she wanted to raise interest rates immediately.

tone_quotes.quote: Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in June indicates that the labor market strengthened and that economic activity has been expanding at a moderate rate.
Near-term risks to the economic outlook have diminished.

for_you.text: Card rates should not move on this decision; a $5,000 balance at about 12.31% APR costs about $51.29 a month in interest.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 1.52% and moved -5 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 3.42% would fall by about $8.31 a month.
Savings yields should stay roughly where they are, since the Fed held rates.
Unemployment was 4.9%, and employers added an average of 162k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 1.1% over the past year (June 2016); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 1.6%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 1.3% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved -2 bp on the day.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved 0.14% on the day.

whats_next: The statement signals that future rate hikes will be gradual as the economy continues to evolve. An educational forecast model assigns a 99% probability of a hold at the next meeting.

citations.detail: Against this backdrop, the Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 1/4 to 1/2 percent.
